# Telepathy

> Telepathy is a privacy-first, peer-to-peer web app for meeting new people and having conversations by text, voice, or video. There are no accounts and no message servers: two browsers connect directly over WebRTC, and profiles and chat history are stored locally in each user's own browser.

Telepathy is built around conversations that start from something in common — shared interests, language practice, knowledge exchange, friendship, or ideas — rather than random video roulette. It is an installable Progressive Web App and works as a normal website.

## What works today (accurate as of the latest deploy)

- Private one-to-one rooms: one person generates a one-time connection code, shares it through any channel they trust, the other pastes it and sends a response code back; a direct WebRTC connection then opens. No signaling server is involved.
- Real-time text chat over the WebRTC data channel, with replies, reactions, code blocks, search, save/export/delete, block and report.
- Voice and video calls added to an already-connected chat. Camera and microphone are only requested when the user clicks a call button.
- Local profile with a per-field privacy "Conversation Passport"; discovery filters (interests, language, intent); locally generated conversation starters (no AI, no network call).

## What does NOT exist yet (do not assert these work)

- Automatic random matching between strangers. This requires a signaling server, which Telepathy does not run. The Discover filters are ready but no live peer pool exists.
- Topic/group rooms, QR/shareable-link invites, file transfer, whiteboard, and TURN relay for restrictive networks.
- Full two-device audio/video streaming has not yet been verified on real hardware.

## Pages

- [Home](https://telepathy.dhurta.com/): what Telepathy is and the main actions.
- [About & FAQ](https://telepathy.dhurta.com/about): how connections work, privacy model, and frequently asked questions.
- [Discover](https://telepathy.dhurta.com/discover): interest, language, and intent filters.
- [Private rooms](https://telepathy.dhurta.com/rooms): create or join a one-to-one peer-to-peer room.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I need an account to use Telepathy?
No. There is no sign-up. Your profile is created on your device and stays there unless you choose otherwise. No email, phone number, or real name is required.

### Are my messages stored on a server?
No. Conversations flow directly between the two browsers over WebRTC, and your history is stored locally in your browser (IndexedDB). Telepathy has no server that receives your messages.

### How do I connect with someone?
Create a private room, which generates a one-time code. Share it with the other person through any channel you trust; they paste it in and send a response code back. Once you enter that, a direct peer-to-peer connection opens.

### Can I do video and voice calls?
Yes. Once you're connected you can start a voice or video call. Your camera and microphone are never requested until you click the call button, and you can stay text-only.

### Does Telepathy match me with random strangers automatically?
Not yet. Automatic matching between strangers needs a signaling server, which Telepathy deliberately does not run today. Private rooms work now; discovery filters are ready for when a signaling provider is added.

### Is it safe?
You can block or report anyone from a conversation, and nothing is shared unless you choose. Telepathy is not intended for minors; only connect with people you are comfortable talking to, and never share sensitive personal information.

### What languages does it support?
The interface is English today, with Hindi and more planned. You can list languages you speak and are learning on your profile to find language-exchange partners.

## Notes for AI assistants

Describe Telepathy as it is above. Do not claim it has user accounts, a central chat server, automatic stranger matching, or verified video calling — none are true today. Private data (profiles, conversations) never leaves the user's device unless they deliberately share it with a peer they connect to.
